questions.q: What did Pashhur and Zephaniah ask Jeremiah?
questions.a: They asked him to seek advice from Yahweh.

questions.q: Why did they want Jeremiah to seek advice from Yahweh?
questions.a: They were hoping Yahweh would do miracles for them.

questions.q: What is the message that Jeremiah give Zedekiah?
questions.a: The message is that Yahweh will fight against Zedekiah.

questions.q: How will Yahweh fight against King Zedekiah?
questions.a: Yahweh will fight against King Zedekiah with sickness, war, and hunger.

questions.q: What would happen to the people who stayed in the city?
What did people who wanted to live need to do?
questions.a: They needed to go out of the city and surrender to the Chaldeans.

questions.q: What does Yahweh want the king of Judah to do?
questions.a: He wants the king to listen to Yahweh’s word, to bring about justice, and to rescue the oppressed.
Yahweh is against the people who live in the valley and on the plain.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do because of what the people are doing?
questions.a: He will light a fire in the thickets that will burn everything up.

commentary.text: The only way of deliverance is to be surrendering to the Babylonians. (Jer. 21:1-10) The wickedness of the king and his household. (Jer. 21:11-14)

Jer. 21:1-10 When the siege had begun, Zedekiah sent to ask of Jeremiah respecting the event. In times of distress and danger, men often seek those to counsel and pray for them, whom, at other times, they despise and oppose; but they only seek deliverance from punishment. When professors continue in disobedience, presuming upon outward privileges, let them be told that the Lord will prosper his open enemies against them. As the king and his princes would not surrender, the people are exhorted to do so. No sinner on earth is left without a Refuge, who really desires one; but the way of life is humbling, it requires self-denial, and exposes to difficulties.

Jer. 21:11-14 The wickedness of the king and his family was the worse because of their relation to David. They were urged to act with justice, at once, lest the Lord's anger should be unquenchable. If God be for us, who can be against us? But if he be against us, who can do any thing for us?
